Remembering Language Movement martyr Rafiq
2008-11-04T00:00:00+06:00 | Zahangir Alam Biswas, Manikganj
https://www.thedailystar.net/news-detail-61695

On the occasion of 81st birth anniversary of Language Movement martyr Rafiquddin Ahmed, a discussion and cultural programme were held in Manikganj recently.

Shaheed Rafiq Smriti Pathagar, a library in memory of the martyr, organised the discussion and cultural programme at the Sangskritik Biplabi Sangha auditorium in the town.

Convener of the organisation, Anha Faruk Khan presided over while Shakila Sabrin Rana, one of the members presented the keynote paper.

Among others, lecturer at Kalusah Degree College, Shamim Ara Rina; assistant teacher, SK Government Girls' School, Irshad Jahan Chowdhury; cultural personality Iqbal Ahmed Kochi and a relative of the martyr, Golenur Begum spoke at the discussion.

Speakers reminisced on Shaheed Rafiq and demanded a central Shaheed Minar in the district at the martyr's home in the Paril village.

In the keynote paper, Rana said the history and culture of this country are often under threat of distortion. She alleged that a textbook published by the board referred to Khudiram as a "terrorist."

On page 62 of the Social Science book for classes nine and ten under the national curriculum and textbook board, refers to Khudiram, an activist during the anti-Raj movemnt, as a terrorist.

On behalf of the organisation, Rana said that they would initiate a signature collection campaign against the distortion of history in textbooks.

The discussion was followed by a cultural programme where local artists Priyanka Roy, Sathi, Bithi, Chapal, Shakila rendered patriotic songs. Local artiste Ali Azam and others recited poems.

Rafiquddin Ahmed was born in Paril under Singair upazila in Manikganj on October 30, 1926. He was the first to be martyred during the Language Movement in 1952.
